model_annotation: Figure 2 is a grouped bar chart illustrating the negative log-probabilities of clinically relevant tokens generated by Mistral-v0.2, comparing the base model with its fine-tuned variants across six medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The horizontal axis categorizes the six specialties, while the vertical axis represents “Negative log-probability” on a linear scale ranging from 22 to 27, with tick marks at intervals of 1. Each specialty group contains two adjacent vertical bars: the left bar (light orange) corresponds to the “Mistral-v0.2-base” model, and the right bar (darker orange) corresponds to the “Fine-tuned” model for that specialty. For all six specialties, the fine-tuned model’s bar is shorter than the base model’s, indicating lower (i.e., better) negative log-probabilities. For example, in the “Cardio” group, the base model’s bar reaches approximately 25.8, while the fine-tuned model’s bar is at about 24.5; similarly, in “Pediatrics,” the base model is near 25.5 and the fine-tuned model is near 24.2. The chart visually demonstrates that fine-tuning consistently improves token probability estimates for clinical terms within each specialty, supporting the paper’s hypothesis that performance gains stem from domain shifting rather than knowledge injection.
